To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a denotational model of programming languages can be constructed in an algebraic setting, that the model is set theoretical, that it can be constructed in a'reverse order' and that it can be used to construct virtual languages, i.e. languages which have no implementation but which can be used to develop programs in a denotational style, which are subsequently implemented in a conventional way.

a denotational model of a virtual language can be constructed in such a manner that the denotations are just sets and the denotational model can be constructed in a layer by layer manner, starting from a denotational domain and proceeding to the abstract syntax, and then to a concrete syntax, which is a programming language.
(i) the denotational model can be constructed in a systematic manner and (ii) it provides a solid foundation for a language design, in particular for a language with a strong type system.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (i) a systematic construction of a denotational model for a programming language, (ii) a construction of a denotation for an API, (iii) a construction of an API for a DBMS, (iv) a construction of denotational semantics for a DBMS.
the following questions: How to construct a language from its semantics? How to construct a denotational model for SQL? How to construct an algebraic framework for denotational semantics?
